The `blowhorn analytics` commands. Each one's `--help` prints the same text.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`analytics activity`](#blowhorn-analytics-activity) | Print one activity's result, read from the store. |
| [`analytics history`](#blowhorn-analytics-history) | Print the follower history the collectors have already recorded, as one dated series read from the store: every LinkedIn page and every profile's X trend, whichever machine collected them. |
| [`analytics import-exports`](#blowhorn-analytics-import-exports) | Read the LinkedIn page content exports already on disk and record each activity's reception figures in the store. |
| [`analytics operations`](#blowhorn-analytics-operations) | Aggregate the run ledger, read from the store, into operations per profile, per platform, per command, per day or per host. |

## blowhorn analytics activity

Print one activity's result, read from the store: for each profile and platform it is addressed to, whether it went out (when, the live link, which computer and browser profile ran it, and on a failure the error and the fix), how it was received where reception is collected (LinkedIn page activities, from the page content exports, with the date the figures were read and a comparison with the page's typical activity), and the follower change around it, labelled derived. Anything not collected says so, with a reason, never as a zero. A computer with no store prints a short explanation and exits 3.

```text
blowhorn analytics activity [OPTIONS] activity
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activity` | yes | Activity number, as `content list` prints it |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string | `all` | Platform scope for `blowhorn analytics`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn analytics activity` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn analytics activity 164 --json
blowhorn analytics activity 164 --profile alex
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn analytics history

Print the follower history the collectors have already recorded, as one dated series read from the store: every LinkedIn page and every profile's X trend, whichever machine collected them. Tolerates the N/A cells the collectors write, and derives the 30-day net, growth rate and (LinkedIn pages only) unfollowed figures, each labelled derived in the output; X profiles carry a net change and no unfollowed count, because X measures only the total. A store that cannot be reached exits 3.

```text
blowhorn analytics history [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--since` | string |  | How far back to read: a number with d, w, m or y (30d, 12m, 1y), or `all` (default: 12m) |
| `--subject` | string |  | One page or profile name (all by default) |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn analytics`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn analytics history` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn analytics history --json --since 12m
blowhorn analytics history --json --subject Acme --since all
blowhorn analytics history --subject alex --since 90d
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn analytics import-exports

Read the LinkedIn page content exports already on disk and record each activity's reception figures in the store: impressions, views, clicks, click-through rate, likes, comments, reposts, follows and engagement rate from each export's All posts sheet, dated by the export. Each activity is matched to its activity by its link; activities made outside Blowhorn are kept and marked unmatched. Prints activities read, matched and stored per file. Safe to run again: a reading lands once per activity and export date. `--dry-run` reads and matches without writing.

```text
blowhorn analytics import-exports [OPTIONS] [paths...]
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paths ...` | no | Export files to read (default: every content export in the analytics folder) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string | `all` | Platform scope for `blowhorn analytics`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn analytics import-exports` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn analytics import-exports
blowhorn analytics import-exports data/analytics/acme_content_20260719_033126.xls --dry-run --json
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn analytics operations

Aggregate the run ledger, read from the store, into operations per profile, per platform, per command, per day or per host: how many runs each action made, what they confirmed, skipped and failed, and which profiles and platforms were active. Reads the ledger only - a dry run is counted apart and never as an operation, and records exist from the first run after this command shipped, so a window older than that reports zero rather than guessing. Per host is the per-machine history now that several machines share one store. A store that cannot be reached exits 3.

```text
blowhorn analytics operations [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--since` | string |  | How far back to read: a number with d, w, m or y (30d, 12m, 1y), or `all` (default: 30d) |
| `--group-by` | string |  | Aggregate per profile, platform, command, day or host -- host is the machine that ran it (default: profile) |
| `--kind` | string |  | Which ledger records to aggregate: run (action runs, the default) or tick (scheduler passes) |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Platform scope for `blowhorn analytics`. One of: bluesky, linkedin, x, all (`all` means every platform listed here) |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn analytics operations` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn analytics operations --json --since 30d --group-by profile
blowhorn analytics operations --json --since 7d --group-by platform
blowhorn analytics operations --kind tick --group-by day --since 14d
blowhorn analytics operations --group-by host --since 30d
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.
